subject: Clarifications: Reservation sizing, GPU mix and tail-latency options for AlphaEdge RFI
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@alphaedge.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: Dedicated reservation sizing for AlphaEdge

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the quick intake form — attached is our RFI template (AlphaEdge-RFI-Template.pdf). We are preparing a procurement packet and need clear guidance on recommended reserved capacity for Redwood Dedicated. High-level profile below:

- Expected steady-state usage: 200k embeddings/day (text-embedding-3-like)
- Peak concurrent generation: up to 10k qps for short-lived chat endpoints during launches (95th percentile request size ~256 tokens)
- Tail-latency target: 99th <= 120ms for short generations; 95th <= 50ms for embeddings
- Percent streaming: ~30% of chat calls require streaming token-by-token
- Model constraints: prefer open models; quantized variants acceptable if quality delta < 2% measured by our evals
- Security: VPC + audit logs required (we will include SOC2 in SOW)

Questions we need answered in the next 3 business days to include in our RFP response:
1) Recommended GPU families and counts for a committed baseline and recommended burst capacity (please provide rationale).
2) Throughput mapping: qps -> GPU slots with assumptions (batch sizes, seq len, KV cache hit rates).
3) Tail-latency tradeoffs and guardrails (how does batching/auto-batching affect 99th).
4) Can you support mixed fleet (e.g., A100 + H100) with routing fallback?
5) Typical reservation phasing you recommend for a two-quarter rollout (min viable reserved pool -> scale plan).

Please attach any modeling sheets or runbooks that help justify the numbers.

Best,
Procurement Team
AlphaEdge Inc.

Attachment: AlphaEdge-RFI-Template.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-27T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: Dedicated reservation sizing for AlphaEdge (throughput modeling)

Avery / Karthik — quick modeling notes and recommended baseline. See attached throughput_modeling_sheet.xlsx for the per-GPU math. Highlights:

1) GPU family recommendation (technical rationale):
   - H100 (80GB) recommended for sustained low-latency generation at high qps when using FP16/INT8 quantization; best headroom for KV-cache heavy chat and long context.
   - A100 (40/80GB) is still cost-effective for pure embedding workloads and for customers prioritizing price over tail-latency.
   - Mixed fleet is feasible: route embeddings to A100s (cheaper) and generation to H100s; Redwood runtime supports model variants with routing policies and graceful fallback.

2) Throughput mapping (assumptions):
   - Embeddings: text-embedding model ~ 120 qps per A100-80 with batch size 64, 95th <= 45ms; for 200k/day (~2.3 qps average) a pool of 1 A100-80 reserved is more than sufficient; baseline recommendation: reserve 1-2 A100s for embeddings to cover spikes and redundancy.
   - Generative chat: using a 70B open model quantized to INT8 on H100: ~120 qps per H100 for short 256-token requests with aggressive batching disabled; with batching enabled throughput can increase to ~300 qps but 99th latency degrades.

3) Mapping to AlphaEdge targets:
   - Peak 10k qps (worst-case launch): if they need to serve 10k concurrent short chat qps with 95th<=120ms, a pure reserved pool would need ~35-85 H100s depending on batching and KV-cache hit rate. The modeling sheet shows:
      - Conservative (low batching, strict 99th): ~85 H100s to keep 99th < 120ms.
      - Optimized (workload-aware batching + prefix caching): ~38 H100s with burst overlay for launches.

4) Tail-latency guardrails:
   - Auto-batching increases average throughput but inflates 99th; recommend per-route latency SLOs with hard caps on batch delay (e.g., max_batch_delay=4ms) and reserved tail slots for real-time routes to avoid queue buildup.
   - Use prefix/KV caching aggressively for chat sessions to reduce compute per request and improve 99th.

5) Burst strategy:
   - Recommend baseline reserved pool sized for typical steady-state + a guaranteed burst overlay (on-demand/dedicated burst capacity) for launches. Example phased numbers below.

Attachment: throughput_modeling_sheet.xlsx

—Marcus

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: procurement@alphaedge.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-27T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood response: Reservation sizing & GPU mix recommendations for AlphaEdge (RFI)

Hi Procurement team,

Thanks for the RFI and the clear traffic profile. Attached you'll find a concise response and our modeling workbook (Redwood_AlphaEdge_RFI_Response.pdf, throughput_modeling_sheet.xlsx). Below are the key recommendations and assumptions so your review team can quickly ingest the tradeoffs.

Executive summary:
- Embeddings: reserve 1 A100-80 as baseline; run embeddings on A100 pool (cost-efficient) with autoscale to 2 for redundancy. Assumes batching of 32–64 for embeddings.
- Generative chat (short responses, 256 tokens avg): two-phase reserved plan:
   Phase 1 (Q1): reserve 6 H100s (steady-state support for pilot customers and predictable latency for primary routes).
   Phase 2 (Q2): increase to 12 H100s reserved; rely on burst overlay (on-demand capacity) to reach launch spikes.
- Launch/burst plan: for events that require sustained 10k qps, we recommend a combined reserved + burst strategy. Our modeling shows a conservative fully-reserved plan would require ~85 H100s (high cost). Instead, Redwood recommends mixing aggressive prefix/KV caching, per-route real-time slots, and a burst overlay sized to your risk tolerance (we can size burst pools per-launch with 48–72 hours notice).

Assumptions and SLOs:
- Latency targets: with Phase 2 (12 H100s + burst overlay) and caching, we can meet 95th <= 50ms for embeddings and typical 95th for chat < 80ms; 99th depends on batching policy — we can meet 99th <= 120ms for prioritized routes by reserving tail slots and limiting max_batch_delay.
- Quantization: we support INT8 quantized variants and can validate quality on your eval sets; recommend a short A/B validation run before committing to INT8 for generation-critical routes.
- Mixed fleet support: yes — we support routing rules to send embeddings to A100s and generation to H100s with automatic fallback to compatible variants.

Recommended next steps:
1) Share tokenization/profile samples and a small eval prompt set so we can run a short INT8 quality check.
2) Schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop (we block time with Marcus for the modeling walkthrough).
3) If the Phase 1 numbers look good, we'll issue a preliminary reservation worksheet and commercial term sheet for your procurement review.

I'll follow up to propose times for the workshop.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_AlphaEdge_RFI_Response.pdf, throughput_modeling_sheet.xlsx

Subject: Re: Redwood response: Reservation sizing & GPU mix recommendations for AlphaEdge (RFI)

Avery — thanks for the rapid and detailed response, and for the modeling workbook. A few quick clarifications before we schedule the workshop:

- We like the Phase 1 -> Phase 2 approach. For planning, procurement prefers to see a recommended hybrid reserved+burst cost delta (est % over baseline) for two scenarios: conservative (minimal caching) vs optimized (aggressive caching + INT8). Can Marcus provide that in the modeling sheet or a one-pager?
- We're open to a mixed fleet (A100 + H100) — can you confirm how session affinity will be handled? We need persistent session affinity for chat to keep KV cache hot; will routing to different GPU families break affinity?
- Tentative procurement timeline: draft SOW by Oct 10, approvals by Oct 28. Does Redwood have a standard draft SOW we can use?

Would Thursday 2027-09-30 at 10:00 PT work for the 60-minute sizing workshop?

Thanks,
Sara Coleman
Cloud Ops Lead
AlphaEdge Inc.
